sol.section: Recommended exact spec diff; interaction with §§3.3 and 4.7
sol.problem: Changing B5 alone does not make the illustrated heterogeneous slot consistently usable through the accepted machine interface. §3.3 defines a register as 'n device-resident wires of one class' and records its class in the ledger; §4.7 requires qreg operands for CC/R wire and region slots. Consider a = qreg.new A 1; b = qreg.new B 1; t = qreg.concat a b; action_call @split (t) () () (). Both allocations fit the witness target, and concat meets every printed precondition, but its required result [A,B] contradicts the single-class register definition. The fragment descriptor cannot resolve that contradiction. The note's placement citations are correct, but its claim that this B5-only repair suffices overlooks this interacting clause.
sol.fix: Extend the exact diff to §3.3: 'A register denotes an ordered sequence of device wires and records each wire's resolved target class. qreg.new cls n and bennett_qreg_new allocate homogeneous sequences of cls. qreg.concat concatenates the wire and class sequences without moving, copying or reallocating wires; qreg.slice selects corresponding subsequences. Reversal restores the prior sequences and identities. Binding to a region slot requires equality with that slot's expanded B5 class vector and, where present, its inherited topology vertices.' The witness concatenates [A] and [B] into [A,B], returns 3 from initial 0, and reversal restores the original clean registers. Alternatively retain homogeneous base registers and explicitly define composite qreg handles with these concatenation, slicing and binding rules; I recommend the ordered class-vector definition.

sol.section: Recommended exact spec diff; Hashes, catalog and consumers
sol.problem: This proposal changes certificate layout, but neither its exact diff nor the shared INDEX publication decisions states how a mixed fat object uses that layout. The standing bennett-4ht check explicitly requires that statement. General claims that North Star scope remains unchanged do not identify the device certificate inventory or preserve the native-host boundary.
sol.fix: Append to §9.4: 'A mixed fat object retains its native host executable and embeds ISA objects only for marked device modules and their device callee closures. B5 descriptors describe those device invocations and bind to their existing object, closure and schedule identities; the device-region certificate inventory does not require entries for every native host function. At the host/device boundary, existing register ids identify operands whose ordered class vectors must match the selected frames. Host-native functions and host process state do not become ISA frame slots.' No new fat-container encoding or launch entry point is required by this repair.

codex.section: Recommended exact spec diff; ISA §3.3 interacting with §§9.4 and 10
codex.problem: The proposed heterogeneous frame is not reconciled with the runtime register model. §3.3 explicitly defines a register as “n device-resident wires of one class” and records its singular class. Yet qreg.concat requires only distinct live non-view registers and preserves their wires without movement. On the witness target, allocate qA with one A wire and qB with one B wire, concatenate them, and bind the result to split's wire[2] slot. The concatenation satisfies its stated preconditions and produces the proposed [A,B] placement, but violates the unchanged register definition. Rejecting it, relabelling a bit, and preserving the heterogeneous result cannot all implement the same amended machine. This is a direct interaction with the new class-vector contract, not a denial of the placement-level B5 defect.
codex.fix: Extend the diff to §3.3: “A register contains an ordered vector of device-resident wires with a resolved class per wire. A single class abbreviates a homogeneous vector. qreg.new retains its requested-class allocation rule. qreg.concat accepts differing operand classes and concatenates their wire/class vectors without movement; qreg.slice inherits the selected sub-vectors. Free and reversal records preserve and restore the complete vector. Region binding preserves that vector, which the selected §9.4 frame must describe.” Add the A/B concatenation witness: the joined register has classes [A,B], split maps 0,1,2,3 to 3,2,1,0, and reversal restores the original wire ordering, classes and handle states. A separately specified heterogeneous register/view mechanism is another viable route; extending the existing qreg model is the smaller repair.

codex.section: Hashes, catalog and consumers; Recommended exact spec diff
codex.problem: The proposal changes certificate layout but contains no mixed-fat-object application statement. INDEX's general assertion that North Star capabilities remain does not state which embedded objects receive these frames or how native host code reaches the fragmented device slot. This fails the council's explicit standing check for certificate-layout changes.
codex.fix: Append to §9.4: “In a mixed fat object, these descriptors apply to device-region invocations in the embedded ISA objects, using the certificate's existing object, closure and invocation bindings. Native host modules remain native and require neither ISA conversion nor B5 frame records. Native host code launches a device CC entry through §10; that entry may concatenate homogeneous registers under §3.3 and bind the resulting ordered class vector to one source interface slot. The slot's fragments describe that binding without splitting its signature. Native process entry, argv/environment and host-library execution remain outside this device-frame inventory.” For the witness, the native host launches a device CC wrapper that joins A[1] and B[1] and invokes split with the single mut:0 slot.
